name: Covenant Recess
description: A mandated three-day paid holiday issued by the GLMZ Corponation Accord in 2196, officially celebrating 'the harmony of labor and enterprise' — in practice, a public relations instrument created in direct response to the 2195 Ward 5 General Work Refusal, in which 80,000 Tier 2 workers staged a spontaneous coordinated absence that cost the Accord an estimated Φ2.4 billion in lost productivity. The holiday includes mandatory 'civic enrichment' programming on corponation-owned media channels, a distributed Φ50 food credit to all registered Tier 1-3 residents, and a ceremonial address by the Accord's rotating Chair. Street culture has repurposed the three days as a period of deliberate non-consumption called 'the Void,' refusing to spend the food credits or engage with any corporate media.
cultural_impact: Covenant Recess has become a cultural Rorschach test for M88 residents — genuinely appreciated by some Tier 2-3 workers as rare rest, bitterly mocked on the Shelf as a bribe, and used by Tier 4-5 corporate families as an occasion for ostentatious charity donations that are fully tax-offset. The Void practice has spread beyond the Shelf and is now observed by an estimated 200,000 residents annually.
key_figures: Accord Chair Mirela Fujimoto-Adeyemi (2196 inaugural address)
Cassiel Dube-Orozco (organizer of the 2195 Work Refusal)
story_hooks: The Φ50 food credits this year have been quietly loaded onto a new mandatory Accord-branded wallet app that harvests spending data — someone needs to get the word out before the credits expire and 400,000 people unknowingly consent.
Cassiel Dube-Orozco, the 2195 Work Refusal organizer, has been missing for three days — starting the day before Covenant Recess, the holiday created in direct response to her action.

A player character is tasked with providing security for the Accord Chair's ceremonial address, only to discover the speech contains a buried policy announcement that will effectively end the Void practice through new 'civic participation' requirements.
date: October 17-19 (anniversary of 2195 Work Refusal end date)
origin_event: The 2195 Ward 5 General Work Refusal, an 11-day spontaneous coordinated work absence by 80,000 Tier 2 workers protesting the Accord's elimination of guaranteed rest-day provisions. The Accord created Covenant Recess the following year as a preemptive labor relations measure.
tier_observations: Tier 1: The Φ50 credit is genuinely needed and used; the holiday itself is viewed with contempt; Void observance is strongest here. Tier 2: Mixed — genuine appreciation for the rest days, deep ambivalence about the corporate framing; Void participation is significant. Tier 3: Largely observed as a leisure holiday; some civic programming engagement; minimal Void participation. Tier 4: Company-organized charity events and media appearances; the holiday is a PR opportunity. Tier 5 (Spire): The Accord Chair's address is a social event; the Φ50 credit is considered a rounding error in their philanthropy portfolios.
